issues.label: Wrongful Conviction / Judicial Error
issues.summary: Innocent person convicted due to systemic failures in investigation, prosecution, defense, or adjudication

circuits.detail: Prosecutorial oversight failed — exculpatory evidence suppressed or ignored in pursuit of conviction
Defense advocacy inadequate — overloaded public defender unable to mount effective challenge to state case
Judicial reasoning compromised by confirmation bias, tunnel vision, or political pressure on bench
Law enforcement extracted false confession through coercive interrogation tactics
Eyewitness memory unreliable — suggestive identification procedures produced false positive identifications
Threat assessment inflated by media pressure, public fear, and political demand for conviction

issues.label: Regulatory Overreach
issues.summary: Administrative agencies exceeding statutory authority or imposing disproportionate regulatory burden

circuits.detail: Regulatory framework expanded far beyond original statutory authorization through aggressive interpretation
Constitutional separation of powers stressed — executive agencies exercising quasi-legislative and quasi-judicial power
Compliance burden so extensive that regulated entities spend more on compliance than on core business function
Procedural complexity reaches levels where even good-faith compliance becomes practically impossible
Regulatory text volume exceeds interpretive capacity — overlapping and contradictory requirements create confusion

issues.label: Access to Justice Crisis
issues.summary: Systemic barriers preventing individuals from meaningfully accessing the legal system to protect their rights

circuits.detail: Legal representation inaccessible — 80% of civil legal needs of low-income Americans go unmet
Court system routing impenetrable to pro se litigants — procedural complexity creates effective barriers to entry
Court system chronically underfunded — years-long backlogs make timely justice impossible
Procedural rules designed for represented parties effectively exclude self-represented litigants from fair process
Settlement and dispute resolution options priced beyond reach of most individuals with legitimate claims
Victim and witness support services inadequate — people in crisis navigating opaque bureaucracy without help

issues.label: Mass Tort / Class Action
issues.summary: Large-scale litigation affecting thousands of claimants from a common wrongdoing requiring coordinated judicial management

circuits.detail: Multi-district coordination strained — thousands of individual claims requiring centralized management and bellwether selection
Court routing systems overwhelmed by volume — case management infrastructure buckles under mass filing
Damages calculation distorted — attorney fee structures may misalign incentives between class counsel and claimants
Settlement pressure enormous — defendant facing existential liability, plaintiffs facing years of delay if no settlement
System stress at maximum — judicial resources consumed by mass litigation at expense of all other cases

issues.label: Constitutional Crisis
issues.summary: Fundamental challenge to constitutional order — separation of powers violated, rule of law threatened, or democratic norms eroded

circuits.detail: Constitutional identity under siege — foundational principles being challenged, reinterpreted, or openly defied
Judicial reasoning unable to resolve crisis within normal legal framework — no precedent for the situation
Precedent memory inadequate — constitutional crisis presents novel fact patterns that existing law cannot address
Law enforcement allegiance uncertain — enforcement agencies caught between competing claims to authority
Prosecutorial oversight paralyzed by political conflict — unable to enforce law impartially when political stakes are existential
Regulatory framework losing legitimacy — agencies uncertain whether current administration will be upheld or overturned

issues.label: Corporate Fraud / White Collar Crime
issues.summary: Systematic financial deception by corporate actors — accounting fraud, securities violations, or consumer deception at scale

circuits.detail: Legal risk detection failed — fraud concealed through complexity, offshore structures, and regulatory arbitrage
Threat to public trust and financial markets detected — systemic risk from widespread corporate dishonesty
Prosecutorial apparatus activated — grand juries, SEC enforcement, and DOJ task forces assembled
Regulatory framework breached — oversight systems that should have prevented fraud were captured, underfunded, or circumvented
Damages and penalties insufficient to deter — corporate fines treated as cost of doing business rather than punishment
Complex coordination required — multi-agency, multi-jurisdiction investigation spanning years and thousands of documents
